text:
sam: Heads up — seeing a sustained rise in tiny-gpu pods stuck Pending in us-west3 for the last ~2h. Pod count ~420 Pending, but nodes show free fractional slots. :eyes:
maya: Link? grafana? which team/namespace?
sam: grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/slots/mini-gpu-pending?orgId=1
summary: lots of 0.125 GPU pods, affinity=required to 'nvlink-group', tainted nodes (gpu:reserved=true:NoSchedule).
jordan: I can see the spike on the scheduler heatmap. Looks like packing fails because the affinity wants colocated NVLink siblings, and our recently added node-pools don't all have labels. Some nodes are labeled nvlink=true, others nvlink=partial.
lee: Confirmed — rollout last night added 8 mixed-gpu racks without nvlink label due to inventory mismatch. They advertise topology but scheduler can't match the strict pod affinity.
fran: Any logs for the failing binds?
sam: Paste from pod describe (truncated):
```
Events:
  Normal  FailedScheduling  2m   default-scheduler  0/128 nodes are available: 128 node(s) had taint {gpu:reserved=true:NoSchedule}, 312 node(s) didn't match pod affinity/selector.
```
maya: That combination (taint + strict affinity) is killing binpacking. Small pods are too picky and get scattered into Pending even though we could co-locate by relaxing constraints.
jordan: Proposed quick mitigation: 1) temporarily mark the new racks as nvlink=partial and add a scheduler plugin rule that treats nvlink=partial as acceptable for tiny pods, 2) add a soft affinity (preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution) patch for the 0.125 GPU workload to reduce strictness.
lee: Ops concern: partial NVLink isn't always safe for large jobs. We need to ensure we don't accidentally break larger gang jobs that truly rely on NVLink.
fran: Can we detect pods by annotation and only relax for single-container, <1 GPU jobs? That seems safe.
jordan: Yes — scheduler can use node-affinity weights + pod annotation filter. Quick k8s patch I tested locally:
```yaml
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: tiny-gpu-soft-affinity
value: 1000
description: "Prefer partial-nvlink for tiny single-gpu pods"
```
But we'll also need a mutating webhook to convert requiredDuringScheduling to preferred for matched pods.
maya: Could we instead run a short remediation job to label nodes correctly (nvlink=true/false) from inventory, so no scheduler plugin changes? That's cleaner but riskier during peak.
sam: Labeling is ideal long-term. Short-term I want an ops-safe rollout to get Pending down. Suggest: 1) Apply webhook to the tiny-pod namespace only, 2) Add node label nvlink=partial to the 8 racks, 3) Run a canary: scale up tiny workload in canary namespace and watch eviction/latency.
lee: I'll do a dry-run labeling script and output candidate nodes. Command: `./scripts/label-nvlink.sh --dry-run --pool=mixed-new-racks`
lee: Also we should watch conntrack/egress — earlier fragmentation incidents correlated with conntrack exhaustion when many tiny pods attached sidecars. Opsbot: check conntrack usage across us-west3?
ops-bot: [automated] conntrack usage in us-west3: 74% (threshold 80%). Top consumers: model-proxy sidecars (72%), metrics-exporter (11%).
fran: Nice. So not yet critical. But we should throttle sidecars for tiny pods as part of remediation to avoid pushing conntrack over threshold when Pending clears and they all bind simultaneously.
jordan: Proposal for rollout plan (15m):
- Step 0: Set cluster autoscaler cooldown to +5m to avoid flapping.
- Step 1: Label 8 racks nvlink=partial (dry-run then apply)
- Step 2: Deploy mutating webhook into tiny-gpu namespaces to relax required->preferred for annotated pods
- Step 3: Monitor Pending count, scheduling latency, conntrack, and cost metrics (per-token-like metric: GPU-minutes)
- Step 4: If regressions, revert webhook immediately and remove labels
sam: +1 to that plan. Keep the webhook changes confined to tiny-pods namespace and rollout in 10% canary first.
maya: I'll own monitoring and alerts. I'll set a Grafana panel alert: Pending tiny-gpu pods > 200 for 5m and conntrack > 85% -> pager to eng-oncall.
lee: I'll run label dry-run now and post results. If all good I'll apply in 10m.
fran: After this, follow-up tasks: - inventory reconciliation to ensure future node pools get correct nvlink label - add scheduler test to CI for mixed-pool scenarios - consider a fractional-slot defragmenter job that tries to coalesce tiny pods onto fewer nodes during slack windows.
sam: Thanks team. Keep updates here. :+1:
